\newcounter{probs}

\textbf{Work must be shown to receive credit. Each problem is worth
4 pts unless stated otherwise.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Use properties of determinants to calculate the determinant of the
following matrices:\begin{multicols}{3}

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrrr}
3 & 0 & 0 & 0\\
4 & 3 & 0 & 0\\
5 & 2 & 1 & 0\\
9 & 8 & 9 & 1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$\xspace \columnbreak\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrrr}
1 & 1 & 1 & 1\\
0 & 0 & 2 & 3\\
0 & 2 & 2 & 2\\
0 & 0 & 0 & 4
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$\xspace \columnbreak\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\item $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrrr}
8 & 3 & 5 & 6\\
3 & 9 & \nicefrac{1}{2} & 7\\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\
2 & 4 & 6 & 7
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$\xspace \columnbreak\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}\vfill
\item Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrr}
1 & 2 & 3\\
0 & 4 & 5\\
1 & 2 & 3
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$ 

\begin{enumerate}
\item Calculate the determinant of $A$ using cofactors. \Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Find $C_{32}$, i.e., $A$'s cofactor for the $3^{\mbox{rd}}$ row
and $2^{\mbox{nd}}$ column.\Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\item Does ${\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^{3}a_{1j}C_{1j}=\sum_{j=1}^{3}a_{3j}C_{3j}}$
for any $3\times3$ matrix?\Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\item Let $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
2 & 3\\
4 & 7
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{r}
x_{1}\\
x_{2}
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{r}
1\\
1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$.\begin{multicols}{2}

\begin{enumerate}
\item Find $x_{1}$ using Cramer's rule.\Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Find $x_{2}$ using Cramer's rule.\Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\end{multicols}\vfill\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\newpage
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are $n\times n$ matrices such that $\det A=5$
and $\det B=-2$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Find $\det AB$.\xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Prove that $\left(AB\right)^{-1}$ exists. \xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\item Find $\det\left(AB\right)^{-1}$.\xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\item Find the characteristic polynomials of the following matrices.

\begin{enumerate}
\item $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrrr}
4 & 4 & 1 & 1\\
0 & 3 & 2 & 1\\
0 & 0 & 2 & 3\\
0 & 0 & 0 & 1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$\Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rrr}
-1 & -2 & 1\\
1 & 3 & 2\\
0 & 2 & 1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$\Xspace\vfill\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\item Find the eigenvalues of the following matrices.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $A$ be a $3\times3$ matrix and $p_{A}(t)=(t+1)(t-2)(t+3)$.
\Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\item Let $A$ be a $2\times2$ matrix and $p_{A}(t)=t^{2}+5$. \Xspace\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\newpage
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Give a definition for either \emph{eigenvalue }\uline{or} a \emph{diagonalizable
matrix (or linear transformation)}\addtocounter{probs}{1}\Xspace
\item {[}15 points{]} Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\begin{array}{rr}
1 & 1\\
0 & -1
\end{array}\end{bmatrix}$. Find the eigenvalues and eigenvectors for $A$. \vfill\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\item Prove the following statement: If $A$ and $B$ are similar matrices
then $\det(A)=\det(B)$. \vfill\addtocounter{probs}{1}
\item {[}Bonus{]} Prove that if $A'$ is obtained from the $n\times n$
matrix $A$ by exchanging two rows then \\
$\det A'=-\det A$ (hint: use cofactors and induction). \vfill
\end{enumerate}
